newsitem.title: UK: Ldn freight - BFI falls again, Pacific market weak.
newsitem.headline: Ldn freight - BFI falls again, Pacific market weak.

text.p: The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) fell seven points to 1,274, due to a continuing slow Pacific sector.
A glimmer of hope was seen from the U.S. Gulf/Japan heavy grain route, which saw business concluded at $21.75 for 54,000 tonnes May 8/17 shipment.
On Thursday, this route was reported done at $21.25 for the same size cargo in May, while on Wednesday it was fixed at $22.
The BIFFEX futures market shrugged off Thursday's bounce and returned to its more familiar easier.
"Yesterday was just a technical bounce following previously significant falls. Now due to a lack of firmer fixtures, we're headed down again," one trader said.
At the close, BIFFEX was five to 14 points below Thursday's finish. Most active May traded last at 1,335, down five. Total volume was 190 lots, with 128 lots done on May.
In the mineral sector business was relatively slow. The only fresh ore trade reported was CSC with 120,000 tonnes ore Tubarao/Kaohsiung June 5-16 at $10.10.
On coal, a 150,000 tonnes cargo Richards Bay/Rotterdam mid June was done at $7.10-$7.15.

Timecharter business saw a number of period charters, with MOSK taking the Karoo 161,183 dwt del Far East mid May for five to seven months at $15,500 daily, and Daiichi taking the Marquesa 70,312 dwt del Japan April 30/May 5 for three to five months redel Far East at $9,950.
